findings.title: Live SQL path still builds DuckDB statements and fails as a parse error
findings.body: UnmarshalSQLCommand, the existing server-side expression entry point, never applies the new disable. NewSQLCommand always calls sql.TablesList (pkg/expr/sql_command.go:30). TablesList interpolates the user expression into a DuckDB statement, SELECT json_serialize_sql('...'), after only doubling single quotes (pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:24-26) and passes that string to RunCommands. The replacement DB always returns an error (pkg/expr/sql/db.go:16), so DuckDB is not executed and CVE-2024-9264 is not currently reachable here, but that stub error is the only control on this path. Every dashboard refresh or alert evaluation then logs at Error with the full SQL and the constructed command (parser.go:28) and again at Warn (sql_command.go:32), and the public error is BadRequest 'error reading SQL command' (sql_command.go:33-35). Instances that had sqlExpressions enabled — the population exposed by the CVE — will flood error logs with query text that may contain sensitive literals and will look like a SQL parser outage rather than an intentional shutdown. enableSqlExpressions is not consulted. Reject at NewSQLCommand/UnmarshalSQLCommand with a dedicated disabled error before any DuckDB statement is built or logged; quote-doubling is not enough if RunCommands is later wired to a real engine.

findings.title: SQL disable helper always returns false and panics if features is nil
findings.body: enableSqlExpressions (pkg/expr/reader.go:194-200) is the only explicit gate added for SQL expressions, but it always returns false: it stores the negation of FlagSqlExpressions and then returns false from both branches. The flag has no effect, yet IsEnabledGlobally is still called before either return. If ExpressionQueryReader.features is nil, that call panics on a nil interface instead of returning a rejection, and only SQL queries hit it — math, reduce, resample, and classic parsing do not touch h.features. Callers also receive fmt.Errorf('sqlExpressions is not implemented') at line 131, which is false: the feature existed and is being turned off for CVE-2024-9264. This helper is not used by UnmarshalSQLCommand, so it does not cover the existing execution path.

findings.title: No regression test that SQL expressions stay disabled
findings.body: This change is the in-repo fix for critical CVE-2024-9264, but no test was added or updated. Nothing asserts that ExpressionQueryReader.ReadQuery rejects QueryTypeSQL even when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled, that a nil FeatureToggles does not panic, that UnmarshalSQLCommand/NewSQLCommand fails closed without Error-logging a serialization failure, or that TablesList and QueryFramesInto cannot execute SQL. Restoring a DuckDB-backed RunCommands, or changing the inverted enableSqlExpressions helper so the flag turns the ReadQuery path back on, would not be caught. Manual checks mentioned in the PR description are not a substitute for a regression test on a patch intended to be cherry-picked across release branches.
